A linear functional on V can be expressed through a bilinear pairing, and pairings on a finite-dimensional space are represented by symmetric matrices, so the dual is naturally the space of those matrices.
An element of the dual takes a vector and returns a scalar, and does so linearly, so the dual consists of exactly the linear maps sending V into its field of scalars.
